title: Earliest Build Order
statement:
A project has `n` tasks and `m` rules "task `u` must be done before task `v`". All tasks are done one at a time. Among all valid orders, take the one that is smallest when compared as a sequence of task numbers (compare the first tasks, then the second tasks, and so on). 

If the rules contradict each other and no valid order exists, print `CYCLE`. Otherwise let `p_1 ... p_n` be that smallest order and print `(1*p_1 + 2*p_2 + ... + n*p_n) mod 1000000007`.

## Input
The first line contains `n` and `m`. Each of the next `m` lines contains `u` and `v` (a rule: `u` before `v`).

## Output
Print `CYCLE`, or the value described above.

## Constraints
- `1 <= n <= 15000`
- `0 <= m <= 15000`
- no rule is listed twice and `u != v`
